decisions.decision: living-show is a mode of resolve-spec-paths.py, not a new script
decisions.why: The resolver already owns requirement_slices, requirements_for_change and the registry load, and already emits this data for the load steps; a new script would grow a third heading parser
decisions.rejected: A living_show.py sibling of living_validate.py, or a pure-prompt command with no script

decisions.decision: Rules are project-wide and keyed by step, normalized in load_living_specs_block
decisions.why: That normalizer is already the one place the registry shape is decided and already tolerates junk without raising; keying by step means there is no precedence to resolve
decisions.rejected: Per-capability rules (needs a merge order nobody asked for) and a separate rules.yml

decisions.decision: Rules reach a step through the resolver call its load node already makes
decisions.why: Both steps shell out to the resolver exactly when the rules are needed and already know how to degrade; riding that call inherits the failure behaviour and costs no extra process
decisions.rejected: Injecting rules at build time into the command bodies, which would need a rebuild whenever a project edits its rules

decisions.decision: The status bar computes claims in-process and reuses speckit.viewSpecDocument to show them
decisions.why: readLivingSpecs and globMatches are already exported and the match is sub-millisecond; the only new plumbing is an optional requirement heading carried through to the viewer
decisions.rejected: A per-file CodeLens (intrusive, heavier) and dispatching living-show --file (forbidden by the spec)

decisions.decision: The indicator hides at zero rather than showing a dimmed count
decisions.why: A persistent zero on every unclaimed file is noise in a bar competing for a few hundred pixels, and absence already reads as nothing claims this
decisions.rejected: Always visible with a dimmed zero

decisions.decision: rules became an owned registry key rather than an unowned one
decisions.why: splice_registry replaces the region spanning the owned keys, so a rules block sitting above capabilities would have been deleted on the next capability add
decisions.rejected: Leaving rules unowned and documenting that it must sit below capabilities

decisions.decision: The status bar keeps its own __statusBarTest export instead of __test
decisions.why: The specs barrel re-exports both modules with export *, and two __test members are an ambiguous export
decisions.rejected: Dropping the barrel export of the status bar module

decisions.decision: living-show got a --capability scope flag alongside --requirement
decisions.why: A heading can exist in two capabilities, and picking one silently would hand a reader another capability rule under the name they asked for
decisions.rejected: Making --requirement take a capability positionally, as the contract first sketched

decisions.decision: The rules dedupe coerces the prior side read off disk
decisions.why: The simplifier's dict.fromkeys raises TypeError on a non-hashable entry, and this is a capture writer that must never fail the run it observes
decisions.rejected: Keeping the explicit membership loop, which tolerated the corrupt entry but also wrote it back unchanged

plan.summary: Three independent slices, each attached to the file that already owns its concern: resolver modes for the terminal reader, a normalized rules block in the registry, and an in-process status bar claim lookup that reuses the spec viewer.
plan.key_finding: Everything this wave needs is already exported or parsed somewhere; the real constraint is that requirement headings are parsed twice (Python and TypeScript) against shared fixtures, so every new reader must go through those two parsers and never a third regex.

implement.summary: living-show reads a requirement from the terminal, a rules block carries house guidance to the spec and plan steps, and the status bar reaches the requirement that describes the open file.

approach: Add --headings/--requirement/--file modes to the existing resolver and a thin living-show command body over them. Normalize an optional project-wide rules block in the registry and let the specify and plan load nodes read their own step's rules from the resolver call they already make. Add a status bar item that matches the active file against the registry in-process and opens the matching requirement through the existing spec viewer.
